# egui-agent-chat

> An egui widget that shows a chat with an `agentai` agent. You create a `ChatPanel` with your
> own `agentai::Agent` and something that spawns tasks on your async runtime, then call
> `chat.ui(ui)` every frame. The widget streams answers in as Markdown, shows reasoning and
> tool calls as collapsible rows, and has an input with Send/Stop. For vision models it also
> sends images. The conversation is a plain `Vec<agentai::Message>`.

Key facts for integrating:

- `agentai` is not re-exported. Add it as your own dependency, from the same `0.3` line this
  crate uses, so that both share one `Agent` type.
- The widget fills the `egui::Ui` it gets, including its own 12 px margins and an input panel
  at the bottom. To share the screen, put it in a side panel or a window.
- `ChatPanel::ui` returns nothing, and there are no events. Read the state with `history()` and
  `is_running()`.
- A turn runs in the background. The widget asks egui for a repaint whenever data arrives, so
  you don't need to drive repaints yourself.
- A turn can be stopped, or it can fail, after the agent has started its reply, meaning it has
  written text or called a tool. Then the exchange so far stays in the history, marked
  "Stopped." or with the error, and the conversation goes on from it. Tool calls without a
  result are left out. If only reasoning or nothing had come yet, nothing is added, and the
  prompt goes back to the input, together with its images.
- Images are off by default. Turn them on with `set_capabilities` only when the model reads
  them.

## Install

```toml
[dependencies]
agentai = "0.3"
egui-agent-chat = "0.1"          # feature `tokio` is on by default
egui = "0.37"
eframe = "0.37"                  # or any other egui integration
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread"] }
egui_extras = { version = "0.37", features = ["all_loaders"] }  # to draw images
```

## Minimal integration (eframe + tokio)

```rust
use agentai::Agent;
use egui_agent_chat::ChatPanel;

struct App {
    chat: ChatPanel,
    // Keep the runtime alive as long as the chat; declare it after `chat` so it drops last
    _runtime: tokio::runtime::Runtime,
}

impl eframe::App for App {
    fn ui(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, _frame: &mut eframe::Frame) {
        self.chat.ui(ui);
    }
}

fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    // agentai picks the provider from the model name ("gpt-4.1-mini", "provider::model", ...)
    // and reads its settings from the environment, e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY.
    // For a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint: Agent::new_with_url(base_url, api_key, system)
    let agent = Agent::new("You are helpful.")?
        .with_model("gpt-4.1-mini")
        .with_max_iterations(12);
    let runtime = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()?;
    let chat = ChatPanel::new(runtime.handle().clone(), agent);
    let app = App { chat, _runtime: runtime };
    eframe::run_native(
        "Chat",
        eframe::NativeOptions::default(),
        Box::new(|cc| {
            egui_extras::install_image_loaders(&cc.egui_ctx); // needed to draw images
            Ok(Box::new(app))
        }),
    )
    .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("{e}"))
}
```

## ChatPanel API

- `ChatPanel::new(spawner: impl Spawn, agent: impl Into<Arc<Agent>>) -> ChatPanel`: pass an
  `Agent`, or an `Arc<Agent>` that the rest of your app shares.
- `ui(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui)`: call it every frame. It also takes in the data that
  streamed since the last frame.
- `ui_with_toolbar(&mut self, ui, add_widgets: impl FnOnce(&mut Toolbar<'_>))`: the same as
  `ui`, plus your own widgets on the left of the toolbar. Call one of the two each frame, not
  both. See "Custom toolbar widgets".
- `send(&mut self, ctx: &egui::Context, prompt: impl agentai::prompt::IntoPrompt)`: sends a
  message from code, with the current history. `prompt` is text or an `agentai::Prompt`, which
  may carry images. A running turn is stopped and replaced. The input uses this method too.
  It does not check images against the capabilities.
- `cancel(&mut self)`: stops the running turn. A reply that has already started stays in the
  history. Otherwise the prompt and images go back to the input, if the input is empty.
- `is_running(&self) -> bool`: whether the agent is working on an answer.
- `history(&self) -> &[agentai::Message]`: every finished turn, including the user's prompts.
- `set_history(&mut self, Vec<agentai::Message>)`: restores a conversation. It stops a running
  turn and clears the input. Pass `Vec::new()` to start a new chat.
- `set_input(&mut self, text: impl Into<String>)`: puts text into the input, e.g. a suggestion.
- `set_send_shortcut(&mut self, SendShortcut)`: picks the key combination that sends. See
  "Input behavior".
- `set_toolbar(&mut self, visible: bool)`: shows or hides the toolbar below the input, which
  holds the Send/Stop buttons. It is shown by default.
- `set_capabilities(&mut self, ModelCapabilities)`: says what the model can read. The default
  is text only. See "Images".
- `attach(&mut self, media: agentai::Media) -> bool`: attaches an image to the message being
  written. It returns `false` and drops the image when the capabilities don't allow it.

You can call any setter at any time, e.g. from your app's settings.

Configure the agent itself (system prompt, model, tools, max iterations) with `agentai`
before you pass it in. To change the agent, create a new `ChatPanel` and move the history
over with `set_history`.

## Saving and restoring history

`agentai::Message` is serde-serializable, so you can store `chat.history()` and later pass it
back with `chat.set_history(saved)`. A good moment to save is when `is_running()` changes from
`true` to `false` and `history().len()` has grown.

## Images

Image support is behind the model capabilities, because a text-only model answers an image
with an error. Turn it on only for vision models:

```rust
use egui_agent_chat::ModelCapabilities;

chat.set_capabilities(ModelCapabilities::default().with_images(true));
```

With images on:

- The user can drop image files (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) on the window. On native platforms
  they are attached automatically. On the web, dropped files are not read yet.
- Your code can attach images with `chat.attach(media)`, or with `toolbar.attach(media)` from
  a toolbar button, e.g. with your own file picker. Build the image with
  `agentai::Media::from_bytes("image/png", bytes)`, and optionally `.with_name("cat.png")`.
- Attached images appear as thumbnails above the input, each with a remove button, and go with
  the next message, even one without text. Sent images appear in the user's bubble.
- `Toolbar::capabilities().images` tells your toolbar whether to show an image button.
- Turning images off with `set_capabilities` removes the images already attached.

To send an image from code without the input:
`chat.send(ctx, agentai::Prompt::text("What is in it?").with_image_bytes("image/png", &png))`.
Drawing images needs image loaders (`egui_extras::install_image_loaders`).

## Tools

Give the agent a toolbox with `agentai` (`Agent::with_toolbox`, the `#[toolbox]` macro, or
built-ins such as `agentai::tool::buildin::CurrentDateAndTimeToolBox`). The chat shows each
call as a row with the tool's name and a status (running / done / failed), its arguments as a
JSON tree, and the result. If a result contains absolute paths to existing PNG, JPEG or WebP
files, they appear as pictures below the call. This needs image loaders
(`egui_extras::install_image_loaders`).

## Context blocks

To attach long material (a file, a selection) to a prompt without flooding the chat, wrap it
with `egui_agent_chat::context_block(title, body)`. The model gets the full text, and the chat
shows it collapsed under its title.

```rust
let prompt = format!("{}\n\nSummarize it.", egui_agent_chat::context_block("notes.md", &notes));
chat.send(ui.ctx(), prompt);
```

`split_context(text)` does the reverse: it returns the blocks (`ContextBlock { title, body }`)
and the remaining text.

## Async runtimes

Turns run as `egui_agent_chat::Task` (a boxed `Send` future) through the `Spawn` trait.
Cancelling doesn't depend on the runtime: a stopped task is aborted.

- `tokio::runtime::Handle` (feature `tokio`, on by default): `runtime.handle().clone()`.
- Any closure `Fn(Task) + Send + Sync + 'static`, for other runtimes:
  `ChatPanel::new(move |task| { my_runtime.spawn(task); }, agent)`.
- `SmolGlobal` and `Arc<smol::Executor<'static>>` (feature `smol`). agentai's HTTP client
  needs a tokio reactor, so these implementations run each task through
  `async_compat::Compat`, which starts a small tokio runtime in the background.
- If you use your own closure on another runtime, wrap the task the same way:
  `move |task| { my_runtime.spawn(async_compat::Compat::new(task)); }`. Without that, requests
  panic with "there is no reactor running".

## Custom toolbar widgets

The toolbar below the input has Send/Stop on the right. Its left side is yours:

```rust
use egui_agent_chat::icons;

chat.ui_with_toolbar(ui, |toolbar| {
    // `toolbar` dereferences to the egui::Ui of the left side (laid out left to right)
    // An image button, only usable when the model reads images
    let images = toolbar.capabilities().images;
    let image_button = egui::Button::new(format!("{} Image", icons::IMAGE_PLUS));
    if toolbar.add_enabled(images, image_button).clicked()
        && let Some(path) = rfd::FileDialog::new().add_filter("PNG", &["png"]).pick_file() // any picker
        && let Ok(bytes) = std::fs::read(&path)
    {
        toolbar.attach(agentai::Media::from_bytes("image/png", bytes));
    }
    // A button that edits the message being written
    toolbar.add_enabled_ui(!toolbar.is_running(), |ui| {
        if ui.button("Summarize").clicked() { /* set your own app state */ }
    });
    if toolbar.button("Be brief").clicked() {
        toolbar.input().push_str(" Answer in one sentence.");
    }
});
```

- The closure runs every frame while the toolbar is shown. Add widgets and react to clicks in
  it, just like other egui code. It may borrow your app's state, because it is not stored.
- `Toolbar::input()` returns `&mut String`, the text in the input. `Toolbar::is_running()`
  says whether the agent is working on an answer.
- `Toolbar::attach(media) -> bool` attaches an image, and `Toolbar::capabilities()` tells
  whether the model reads images. See "Images".
- To send something yourself, set a flag in the closure, then call `chat.send(ctx, prompt)`
  after `ui_with_toolbar` returns. While it runs, the closure cannot borrow `chat`.
- `set_toolbar(false)` hides the whole toolbar, your widgets included. The closure then does
  not run.

## Icons

`egui_agent_chat::icons` holds the Lucide icon font that the widget uses. It installs itself
on the first frame. To use the icons elsewhere earlier, call `icons::install(ctx)`, then mix
the constants into text: `format!("{} Send", icons::SEND)`.

## Input behavior

`egui_agent_chat::SendShortcut` picks the key combination that sends. The other Enter
combinations add a line. Empty messages are never sent.

- `SendShortcut::Enter` (default), for mostly one-line messages: Enter sends, Shift+Enter
  adds a line.
- `SendShortcut::ShiftEnter`, for mostly multi-line messages: Shift+Enter sends, Enter adds a
  line.
- `SendShortcut::Custom(egui::KeyboardShortcut)`, e.g.
  `KeyboardShortcut::new(Modifiers::COMMAND, Key::Enter)` for Cmd/Ctrl+Enter. Enter adds a
  line.

The placeholder in the empty input names the current shortcuts. While the agent runs, the
toolbar's Send button becomes Stop. If you hide the toolbar with `set_toolbar(false)`,
messages are sent only with the shortcut, and only `cancel()` stops an answer. Give your
users another way to stop, e.g. a menu item.
